verifications.claim: An Individual Retirement Account (IRA) is a tax-advantaged personal savings account allowing individuals to invest for retirement independent of employer-sponsored plans.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Individual Retirement Accounts (IRA) are tax-advantaged investment accounts that individual investors can open to help save for retirement.'; R2: 'An individual retirement arrangement (IRA) is a tax-favored personal savings arrangement, which allows you to set aside money for retirement.'; R3: 'an IRA — is a specialized account that allows you to save and invest for retirement, separate from any employer-sponsored retirement plan'; R10: 'An IRA is a tax-advantaged account designed to help you save for retirement on your own, independent of an employer.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly define IRA as tax-advantaged personal savings/investment for retirement, independent of employer plans.

verifications.claim: Traditional IRAs offer tax-deferred growth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'You pay no taxes on IRA earnings until retirement'; R2: 'Amounts in your traditional IRA, including earnings, generally aren't taxed until distributed'; R4: 'Traditional IRAs provide tax-deferred growth'; R10: 'growth is tax-deferred'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state tax-deferred growth or no taxes on earnings until withdrawal for Traditional IRAs.

verifications.claim: Roth IRAs offer tax-free growth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Income earned on the account... and withdrawals are generally tax-free'; R2: 'Earnings on qualified distributions ... also aren't subject to tax'; R4: 'Roth IRAs offer tax-free growth'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm tax-free growth for Roth IRA earnings.

verifications.claim: IRA contributions require having earned income.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'must have taxable compensation, such as wages...'; R3: 'Anyone who receives earned income can open and contribute to an IRA'; R4: 'Anyone with earned income can contribute'; R10: 'Available to anyone with earned income'
verifications.reasoning: All sources specify earned/taxable compensation required for contributions.

verifications.claim: 2026 IRA contribution limit is $7,500 per year.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'under age 50, you can contribute up to $7,500'; R5: 'up to $7,500 per year'; R6: 'For 2026, the limit is $7,500'; R8: '$7,500 ($8,600 if age 50 and over)'; R9: '$7,500 for 2026'; R10: '$7,500 for 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm $7,500 as the 2026 base IRA limit (under age 50).

verifications.claim: 2026 IRA contribution limit for individuals age 50 or older is $8,600.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'age 50 or older, you can contribute up to $8,600'; R5: '$8,600 for those age 50 and older'; R6: '$8,600 if aged 50 and older'; R8: '$8,600 if you're age 50 and over'; R9: '$8,600 if 50 and over'; R10: 'additional $1,100 for 2026' (7500+1100=8600)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state $8,600 catch-up limit for 2026 age 50+.

verifications.claim: Traditional IRA contributions may be tax-deductible.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Contributions typically are tax-deductible'; R2: 'You may be able to deduct some or all of your contributions'; R4: 'You can generally claim your contributions as a tax deduction'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated as tax-deductible (with possible limits).

verifications.claim: Tax-deductible Traditional IRA contributions reduce current taxable income.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'claim your IRA deduction on Form 1040'; R9: 'put $3,000 in a traditional IRA, you will generally receive a deduction against your $40,000 of income'
verifications.reasoning: Deduction directly reduces taxable income, as standard and exemplified.

verifications.claim: Traditional IRA earnings grow tax-deferred.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'You pay no taxes on IRA earnings until retirement'; R2: 'including earnings, generally aren't taxed until distributed'
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of tax-deferred earnings growth.

verifications.claim: Traditional IRA withdrawals in retirement are taxed as ordinary income.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Distributions from a traditional IRA are fully or partially taxable... fully taxable'; R4: 'You'll pay ordinary income tax on withdrawals'
verifications.reasoning: Withdrawals taxed as ordinary income.

verifications.claim: Roth IRA contributions are made with after-tax dollars.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'made with after-tax dollars'; R3: 'pay income tax on your money before you deposit it'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly after-tax contributions.

verifications.claim: Roth IRA contributions have no immediate deduction.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Contributions to a Roth IRA aren't deductible'; R4: 'Contributions are not deductible'
verifications.reasoning: No tax deduction for contributions.

verifications.claim: Roth IRA earnings grow tax-free.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Income earned on the account... generally tax-free'; R4: 'tax-free growth'
verifications.reasoning: Tax-free growth of earnings.

verifications.claim: Qualified Roth IRA withdrawals in retirement are entirely tax-free.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Earnings on qualified distributions ... aren't subject to tax'; R4: 'tax-free withdrawals'
verifications.reasoning: Qualified withdrawals tax-free.

verifications.claim: IRAs are opened through financial institutions such as banks, mutual fund companies, or stockbrokers.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'set up an IRA with a bank, insurance company, or other financial institution'; R3: 'credit unions and banks... brokers, mutual fund providers'; R11: 'bank... mutual fund stockbroker'
verifications.reasoning: Examples match exactly.

verifications.claim: Earned income for IRA contributions includes wages, salaries, and self-employment income.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'taxable compensation, such as wages, salaries... net income from self-employment'
verifications.reasoning: Direct list includes specified types.

verifications.claim: Anyone can open a traditional IRA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'You can set up an IRA with a bank...'; R3: 'You can open... a traditional IRA regardless of your income'; R4: 'anyone with earned income can contribute' (implies opening)
verifications.reasoning: Sources indicate broad eligibility to open/setup, tied to earned income for contributions but not explicitly barring opening.

verifications.claim: Roth IRA contribution eligibility depends on modified adjusted gross income (MAGI).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'reduced—or even eliminated—based on your modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)'; R5: 'depends on your Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI)'; R8: 'based on modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit MAGI dependence for Roth eligibility.

verifications.claim: Traditional IRA contribution deduction eligibility depends on modified adjusted gross income (MAGI).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'income can impact whether or not you're able to deduct your contributions'; R8: 'varies, depending on your MAGI'
verifications.reasoning: Deductibility phased by MAGI.

verifications.claim: Withdrawing earnings or contributions from a Traditional IRA before age 59½ often triggers a 10% penalty plus taxes.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'made prior to age 59½ ... subject to an additional 10% tax'; R3: 'before age 59½... ordinary income taxes... 10%'; R4: '10% federal penalty tax on withdrawals of both contributions and earnings'
verifications.reasoning: Standard early withdrawal rule confirmed.

verifications.claim: IRA annual contribution limits are lower compared to 401(k) plans.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: '401(k)s allow higher annual contributions (up to $19,500)'; R7: 'lower contribution limits than workplace savings plans, such as 401(k)s'; R8: 'IRA $7,500 vs 401k $24,500'
verifications.reasoning: Direct comparisons show lower IRA limits.

verifications.claim: IRAs do not receive employer matching contributions unlike 401(k)s.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Employers can also make contributions to 401(k)s'; R7: 'Unlike workplace retirement plans'; R10: 'independent of a workplace plan'
verifications.reasoning: IRAs individual, no employer matching; 401(k)s have it.

verifications.claim: SEP IRA is for self-employed individuals or small business owners.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'employer, typically a small business or self-employed individual'; R3: 'businesses of any size, including self-employed individuals'
verifications.reasoning: Directly described for self-employed/small businesses.

verifications.claim: SEP IRA allows higher contribution limits.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: '25% of your annual compensation or $58,000'; R7: 'up to 25% ... up to a maximum of $69,000'
verifications.reasoning: Higher limits (e.g., 25% comp) vs standard IRA $7,500.

verifications.claim: SIMPLE IRA is a retirement plan for small businesses.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Available to small businesses'; R3: 'Designed for small companies'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly for small businesses.

verifications.claim: SIMPLE IRA allows both employer and employee contributions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'allows employer and employee contributions'; R3: 'allow employees and employers to contribute'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states both employer and employee contributions.
